name: Sweden
description: Sweden offers a high quality of life, competitive salaries, and a robust social welfare system, making it an attractive destination for expats. The country is known for its strong emphasis on work-life balance, environmental quality, and efficient public services, though recent changes to citizenship and work permit rules introduce stricter requirements.
longdescription: Expat life in Sweden is characterized by a high standard of living, strong public services, and excellent infrastructure. The economy is highly developed, driven by manufacturing, IT, and environmental innovation, leading to a strong labor market with competitive salaries, particularly in high-demand sectors like IT, healthcare, engineering, and green technologies. Swedes value work-life balance, punctuality, and social equality. The culture can be perceived as reserved initially, but social integration is encouraged through activities like 'fika' (coffee breaks) and participation in clubs. Housing in major cities like Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö can be expensive, but overall living costs are manageable depending on lifestyle and location. Healthcare and education systems are highly developed and publicly funded, providing universal access to residents. However, navigating the bureaucratic processes and adapting to the climate and cultural nuances can be challenging for some newcomers.

visas.name: Swedish work permit (Sweden)
visas.description: The Swedish work permit allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens to live and work in Sweden. It is an employer-initiated permit tied to a specific role, salary, and requires an employment contract. The process is primarily online through the Swedish Migration Agency (Migrationsverket). A new processing model introduced in January 2024 aims to shorten processing times, especially for highly qualified workers.
benefits: Right to work and reside in Sweden for the duration of the permit.
Opportunity to apply for permanent residency after four years of employment.
Family members (spouse/cohabitee and children) can apply for residence permits at the same time.
Renewable permit, allowing for longer stays.
Faster processing times for highly qualified workers (Category A).
visas.path_to_residency_description: A permanent residence permit may be granted after four years of continuous employment in Sweden within a seven-year period. After five years of legal and continuous residence, applicants may also be eligible for EC long-term residence status.
required_documents: Valid passport (copy showing personal data, photo, signature, passport number, issuing country, validity period, and any permission to live in countries other than your country of origin).
Signed employment contract (must specify job title, duties, salary, working hours, and duration).

Documents showing comprehensive health insurance (if employment is for a maximum of one year). For longer stays, employer-provided health, life, occupational injury, and pension insurance must be in place from day one.
Trade union opinion (utlåtande) from the relevant trade union (typically provided by the employer).
Evidence of job advertisement on the EURES portal for at least 10 days (typically provided by the employer).
Academic credentials and CV (translated into Swedish or English if needed).
Documents for accompanying family members, if applicable.

visas.name: Sweden Student Residence Permit
visas.description: The Sweden Student Residence Permit (Uppehållstillstånd för studier) is required for non-EU/EEA citizens intending to study in Sweden for more than three months. It allows recipients to reside in Sweden for full-time higher education studies at an accredited university or university college. As of June 11, 2026, new rules include limitations on working hours (maximum 15 hours per week for bachelor's and master's students), higher requirements for academic progress, and the obligation to notify the Migration Agency of a Swedish address.
benefits: Right to reside in Sweden for the duration of studies.
Allows part-time work (up to 15 hours/week for bachelor's/master's level students from June 11, 2026; unlimited for those with permits before this date) without a separate work permit.
Renewable if studies continue and satisfactory academic progress is maintained.
Possibility to apply for an extended residence permit to seek employment after graduation.
Access to public healthcare if registered in Sweden (typically for permits longer than one year).
visas.path_to_residency_description: Students who complete higher education can apply for a residence permit to look for work or start a business in Sweden for up to 12-18 months. After securing employment, they can apply for a work permit. Permanent residency can be obtained after living and working in Sweden for a total of 5 years (including post-study work). Doctoral students have an accelerated path, potentially gaining permanent residence after three to four years of continuous residence.
required_documents: Valid passport (copy of personal data pages, valid for the entire permit period).
Admission decision from the higher education institution (confirming final admission to full-time, on-site studies).
Proof of paid tuition fees (if applicable, must be paid before applying).

Documents showing financial means to support yourself (e.g., bank statements in your name, scholarship letter, or loan certificate, showing at least SEK 10,314 per month for the duration of the permit).
Documents showing comprehensive health insurance (if studies are for less than one year and not registered in Sweden's population register).
Certified translations of documents not in Swedish or English.

visas.name: Sweden Family Reunification Residence Permit
visas.description: The Sweden Family Reunification Residence Permit allows non-EU/EEA family members to join their relatives (sponsors) who have a residence permit (permanent, work, refugee, or subsidiary protection) or Swedish/Nordic citizenship in Sweden. Eligible family members typically include spouses, registered partners, cohabiting partners, and children under 18 years of age. Both the applicant and the sponsor must generally be over 21 years old. The sponsor in Sweden must meet maintenance requirements, demonstrating sufficient income and adequate housing for the entire family.
benefits: Enables family members to live together in Sweden.
Spouses and partners generally have the right to work in Sweden.
Children gain access to Sweden's public schooling and healthcare system.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency after a qualifying period.
Permit is renewable, offering long-term stability.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Family members are initially granted a temporary residence permit, typically for up to two years. After residing in Sweden for a continuous period, usually four years, they may become eligible to apply for a permanent residence permit. For spouses/partners who lived together for at least two years in their country of origin, a permanent residence permit may be granted directly.
required_documents: Valid passport for the applicant
Proof of family relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate, population registration certificates, joint rental contract, proof of cohabitation)
Documents demonstrating the sponsor's income (e.g., employment contract, salary specifications, bank statements)
Documents proving adequate housing (e.g., rental contract, title deed)
Power of attorney (if someone is applying on behalf of the family member)
Comprehensive private health insurance (required if the total continuous period of residence permits in Sweden is less than one year, or until registered in the Swedish population register).

visas.name: Sweden Self-Employment Permit
visas.description: The Sweden Self-Employment Permit (Residence Permit for Self-Employed Persons) is for non-EU/EEA citizens who wish to live in Sweden and run their own business. Applicants must own at least 50-51% of the business and have executive responsibility for its operations. The business must be viable and focused on selling goods or services within the Swedish market.
benefits: Ability to live and work in Sweden.
Run and manage your own company in Sweden.
Potential path to permanent residency after two years.
Family members can be included in the application.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After an initial permit for up to two years, applicants can apply for permanent residency. This requires demonstrating that the business is successfully supporting the applicant, adhering to generally accepted accounting principles, holding all necessary business permits, and that the applicant has primarily resided in Sweden during the permit period.
required_documents: Valid passport copies (showing personal data, photo, signature, passport number, issuing country, validity period, and any permits to reside in other countries).
Bank certificates or statements showing sufficient funds (SEK 200,000 for main applicant, SEK 100,000 for spouse/partner, SEK 50,000 per child) to support self and family for two years.
Business plan and financial forecasts proving commercial viability.
Evidence of significant industry experience and qualifications.
Proof of previous experience running a business.
Documented knowledge of Swedish or English.
Documents showing ownership of at least 51% of the business (e.g., certificate of incorporation, partnership agreement, share register).
Contracts with customers, suppliers, and for business premises.
Purchase contract and proof of payment if buying an existing business.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A child born to at least one Swedish parent automatically acquires Swedish citizenship, regardless of their birthplace. The same rule applies to people adopted by Swedes. For those born outside Sweden before April 2015 to a Swedish father and foreign mother, citizenship by descent may be obtained if under 18 and paternity is proven. Since 2001, Sweden permits dual citizenship without restrictions.

Naturalization.desc:
As of June 6, 2026, the general rule requires applicants to have lived in Sweden for at least eight years (up from five years) with continuous lawful residence.

Applicants must also demonstrate:
*   **Self-sufficiency:** Be able to support themselves through their own stable income, corresponding to at least three income base amounts per year (approximately SEK 20,000 per month before tax for 2026), and not have received social assistance for more than six months in the past three years.
*   **Knowledge of Swedish and Swedish Society:** Mandatory for applicants aged 16 to 66, typically proven through a passing grade in Swedish for Immigrants (SFI course D) or a citizenship test.
*   **Orderly Life:** Stricter requirements apply, meaning applicants must have lived a well-behaved and honest life, with longer waiting periods after any crimes or misconduct.

Exceptions to the eight-year rule include:
*   Nordic citizens or former Swedish citizens: 2 years.
*   Stateless persons: 5 years (previously 4 years).
*   Refugees: 7 years (previously 4 years).
*   Individuals under 21 years of age: 7 years.
*   If identity cannot be proven: at least 10 years.

Birthright.desc: Sweden does not grant birthright citizenship (jus soli). Citizenship is primarily acquired through descent from a Swedish parent (jus sanguinis). Only stateless children born in Sweden may be able to acquire citizenship through notification.

Spouse and Family.desc: As of June 6, 2026, if married to, in a registered partnership with, or cohabiting with a Swedish citizen, the residency requirement is 7 years (previously 3 years). Additionally, the couple must have lived together for at least five years, and the Swedish partner must have been a Swedish citizen for five years. Family members (spouses, registered partners, and children under 18) of work permit holders are generally eligible for residence permits. Children will now need to submit their own citizenship applications, rather than being included in a parent's application.

tax_advice:
*   **Tax Residency:** Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed only on Swedish-source income. Residency is triggered by a permanent home or continuous stay for 6+ months.
*   **Personal Income Tax:**
    *   **Municipal Tax (Kommunalskatt):** This is the main component, averaging approximately 32.38% in 2026, but varies by municipality (e.g., Stockholm ~30.66%, Malmö ~33.06%).
    *   **National Tax (Statlig Skatt):** A 20% national income tax applies to earned income exceeding SEK 643,000 per year in 2026. The top marginal rate can reach approximately 52-55% for high earners.
    *   **Basic Allowance (Grundavdrag):** An income-dependent basic deduction ranging from SEK 17,400 to SEK 45,600 annually for residents.
    *   **Expert Tax Relief:** Qualifying foreign specialists, researchers, and executives can benefit from a 25% income exemption from income tax and social contributions for up to 7 years.
    *   **SINK (Special Income Tax for Non-Residents):** For non-residents working temporarily (under 6 months) or commuters, a flat tax rate of 22.5% on Swedish-source employment income applies from January 1, 2026 (further reduced to 20% from January 1, 2027).
    *   **Social Security Contributions:** Employers pay 31.42% of the gross salary.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The corporate income tax rate is a flat 20.6% on all corporate profits for 2026. Resident companies are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed on Swedish-source earnings.
*   **VAT (Value Added Tax):**
    *   Standard rate is 25% on most goods and services.
    *   Reduced rate of 12% applies to hotel accommodation, restaurant meals, and some foodstuffs (excluding alcoholic beverages).
    *   A 6% rate applies to books, public transport, newspapers, and certain cultural/sports events.
    *   **Temporary VAT reduction on food:** From April 1, 2026, through December 31, 2027, the VAT rate on most food products and bottled water is temporarily reduced from 12% to 6% (excluding alcoholic beverages and tap water).
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Generally a flat rate of 30% on gains from the sale of shares, interest, and dividends.
*   **Real Estate Tax:** A local government charge of 0.75% of the tax assessment value for detached/semi-detached houses, with a maximum of SEK 10,425 per year.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** A single person can expect to spend around $1,114 - $1,837 per month excluding rent, while a family of four needs approximately $4,140 - $4,219, excluding rent. Stockholm is the most expensive city for rent, with a one-bedroom apartment in the city center averaging $1,628-$2,170.
*   **Language:** While many Swedes speak excellent English, learning Swedish (SFI - Swedish for Immigrants) is highly recommended for daily life, deeper integration, and career opportunities.
*   **Safety:** Sweden ranks high in personal and public safety.
*   **Registration:** Upon arrival, EU/EEA citizens should register with Skatteverket for a 'personnummer' (personal identity number) once they have an address and employment contract. Non-EU citizens will need to apply for relevant permits first.
*   **Housing:** Start searching for housing well in advance, as the market, especially in major cities, can be competitive. Websites like Blocket Bostad and Qasa, or expat Facebook groups, can be useful.
*   **Punctuality:** Swedes highly value punctuality in both professional and social settings.
*   **Work Permits:** As of June 1, 2026, new work permit rules include a salary requirement of at least 90% of the median salary in Sweden (approximately SEK 33,390 per month in April 2026). Employers must also notify the Swedish Migration Agency if an employee hasn't started within four months of being granted a permit.
